goal: Integrate Gmail into an existing web system so the admin can view and reply to customer inquiries without leaving the admin panel.
constraints: Framework-agnostic. Do NOT assume Laravel, PHP, Node.js, or any specific stack.
First step of implementation must be inspecting the actual project codebase to detect the real stack.
core_principle: Gmail is the source of truth (the real mailbox). The application's database is a synchronized local copy that the admin UI reads from. The admin panel should almost never call the Gmail API just to render data that's already synced.

customer: Inquiry is received by the configured Gmail account
Continues using their normal email client
If admin replies via the panel, customer receives it as a normal email
If customer replies to that email, it eventually appears in the admin panel
admin: Opens the email/inquiry section of the admin panel
Sees emails already stored in the app's database (no live Gmail call)
Replies from inside the admin panel
Reply is sent out through the Gmail API
Customer replies are synced from Gmail back into the database automatically

initial_sync.purpose: Populate the DB with existing Gmail messages once.
initial_sync.example: 200 existing messages -> fetched once and stored.
initial_sync.rule: Never re-download the same historical messages on every inbox load.

incremental_sync.method: Gmail API history.list using a stored historyId — not a full mailbox refetch.
logic: Store the latest historyId after every successful sync
When notified of a change, call history.list with the stored historyId
Only fetch the specific new/changed messages returned
incremental_sync.fallback: If the stored historyId is too old / expired on Gmail's side, fall back to a full resync.

push_notifications.technology: Gmail API watch() + Google Cloud Pub/Sub
flow: Gmail publishes a Pub/Sub notification containing a new historyId
Backend calls history.list with the previously stored historyId
Backend fetches only the required message details (messages.get)
operational_notes: watch() subscriptions expire and must be renewed periodically
Push delivery can be delayed or dropped — implement a periodic polling fallback
If stored historyId is stale/invalid, trigger a full resync

admin_inbox_read_rule.rule: Opening the inbox = a DB query, ordered by received date. No Gmail API call required.
benefits: Supports app-specific fields (assignment, tags, internal status) that Gmail doesn't have

gmail_api_quotas.note: Quotas are measured in quota units, not raw request counts. These are three separate limits with different scopes/time windows, not interchangeable.
gmail_api_quotas.practical_takeaway: For a small site with a handful of inquiries/day, quota is a non-issue if sync is implemented efficiently (history-based, not full refetches).

database_design.dedup_rule: Use gmail_message_id and gmail_thread_id as the identity keys — never duplicate a message already synced.

conversation_threading.rule: Group messages by threadId in the admin UI instead of showing every email as a standalone item.
conversation_threading.customer_reply_handling: New message with a matching threadId gets appended to the existing conversation, not created as a new one.

admin_to_customer: Backend sends via Gmail API (messages.send), correctly threaded to the Gmail conversation
Backend stores/syncs the sent message into the local DB
customer_to_admin: Customer replies normally from their own email client
Backend fetches and stores the new message
Admin sees it appear in the panel

implementation_order: Inspect the existing project to determine actual backend/frontend stack
Create DB tables: synced messages + gmail_sync_state
Set up Gmail API OAuth for the mailbox account
Store synced messages in the DB
Build admin inbox UI reading only from the DB
Implement admin replies via Gmail API
Add periodic sync as a fallback safety net
Test: customer inquiry -> Gmail -> DB -> admin panel
Test: admin reply -> Gmail -> customer inbox
Test: customer reply -> Gmail -> sync -> admin panel

do_not: Build a full helpdesk platform unless explicitly requested
Assume Laravel or any specific framework
Add advanced email features before basic sync + reply flow is solid
scope_guardrails.v1_goal: A reliable Gmail-to-database sync plus a working admin inbox/reply loop — nothing more.
